pairs.subject: background-jobs
pairs.evidence: crates/api/src/schedule_sweep.rs:66 The schedule sweep (and the storage maintenance sweep at crates/api/src/storage.rs:295) is a detached tokio task whose JoinHandle is dropped: there is no registration door, no roster, no stop handle and no graceful drain. A panic in the async tick body silently ends the loop, with nothing on the health surface to show it.

techniques.evidence: crates/api/src/schedule_sweep.rs:66 Detached spawn, JoinHandle discarded; main.rs:528-548 arms five such loops independently (ad-hoc timer swarm), and axum::serve has no graceful-shutdown drain or supervisor stop sequence.

crates/api/src/schedule_sweep.rs:81 The tick body runs with no crash barrier (catch_unwind / a supervised JoinHandle) and no per-tick deadline, so a panic kills the loop silently and a hung store call wedges it. There is no consecutive-failure backoff or quarantine. Per-schedule errors are caught, and the sequential await means ticks cannot re-enter.

crates/api/src/schedule_sweep.rs:117 The schedule sweep writes no per-tick snapshot: it emits a log line only when it fired, so 'ran and found nothing' and 'did not run' look identical. health.rs has no loop liveness. The storage sweep does better, with a bounded flight-recorder ring of ran/nothing_to_do/deferred/failed outcomes at storage.rs:265, but the subject requires this of every loop.

crates/api/src/schedule_sweep.rs:112 A schedule whose fire() errors before save() keeps an overdue next_due, so the same warning is written every 60s tick for as long as the fault stands. There is no previous-set diff.

crates/api/src/schedule_sweep.rs:68 Fixed-delay rather than catch-up burst, and the interval is floored by MIN_SECS where it is parsed (line 51). The storage loop's activity-gauge gate makes its work state-dependent. Missing: jitter and a dual active/idle rate, both minor at a 60s cadence.

crates/api/src/schedule_migrate.rs:9 The idempotent migration runs before the first sweep. Overdue schedules collapse to one firing via advance_from(now). Orphaned running jobs are reclaimed by lease staleness (jobs.rs:108) on the same path the steady state uses. Weak spots: catch-up firings are not attributed as sweep-driven, and the migration is uncapped.

crates/api/src/jobs.rs:128 Jobs are keyed by id. Cancel works in two steps (cancelling → cancelled), cooperatively at case boundaries with partial results marked. Terminal states are distinct, a finished job returns 409, and get_job gives a snapshot. Progress is a free-form string rather than a declared done/total unit.
crates/api/src/jobs.rs:108 This context has no bounded wait on a tracked operation. Claim is a non-blocking poll, and the stale window is a lease-detection bound, not a collector's wait budget.
crates/api/src/storage.rs:297 These loops do housekeeping (maintenance, schedule firing). Their first output is incidental, and they are not the only writer of state that readers need.
crates/api/src/schedule_migrate.rs:21 Loop start is infallible (a spawn), and startup work deliberately never fails the start, so there is no failed-start state to keep.
